Good news on the account side: the $65.00 payment has gone through — bill B1234321 now shows as **Paid** — and your line 555-123-2002 is **Active**, so the suspension is fully cleared. That means the remaining problem is on the device itself.

The clue is in what you described: the status bar is showing the **✈️ Airplane Mode** icon and **no signal bars**. Airplane Mode turns off all of the phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so it will keep you at "No Service" no matter how healthy the line is.

**Please try this:**

1. Open your phone's quick settings by swiping down from the top of the screen (on some phones, swipe down twice).
2. Find the **Airplane Mode** tile — it will be highlighted/on.
3. Tap it to turn Airplane Mode **OFF**. The ✈️ icon should disappear from the status bar.
   
   *(Alternatively: Settings → Network & Internet → turn off Airplane Mode.)*

4. Wait about 30 seconds and look at the top-left of your screen — you should now see signal bars plus a network type like "5G" or "LTE".

Then try making a call or loading a web page again.

Let me know whether the ✈️ icon clears and signal bars appear after that. If Airplane Mode is already off in settings but the icon is stuck on, tell me and we'll take it from there.

turns.thought:
I hear you, John — you've done everything right on your end, and I appreciate your patience. Yes, the SIM card is the right next step. Your line is **Active** and the bill is **Paid**, so the account side is fully clear; a "No Signal" reading with every switch correct points to the phone not properly reading the SIM.

**Reseating the SIM card:**

1. Power the phone completely **off** (hold the power button, then slide/tap Power off). Wait until the screen is fully black.
2. Locate the **SIM tray** — usually on the left or right edge of the phone, with a tiny pinhole next to it.
3. Insert the **SIM eject tool** (or a straightened paperclip) into the pinhole and press firmly until the tray pops out slightly.
4. Pull the tray out gently and remove the SIM card.
5. Check the card and the tray:
   - Make sure the card is sitting **flat** and oriented correctly in the tray (gold contacts facing down, notched corner aligned with the tray's notch)
   - Make sure there's no obvious dust or debris on the gold contacts — if there is, wipe them gently with a dry, soft cloth
   - Make sure nothing looks bent or damaged
6. Reseat the card firmly into the tray, then push the tray back into the phone until it clicks flush with the frame.
7. Power the phone back on and wait about 60 seconds.

Then check the status bar again and let me know whether signal bars appear.

**One important note:** while the phone is off, also glance at the SIM card itself — if you see it's cracked, badly scored, or the gold contacts are worn, tell me and we'll go down the replacement route instead.

Also, to set expectations: your device (Smartphone Pro Max) is eSIM-capable, so if the physical SIM reseat doesn't bring the signal back, moving your line to an eSIM profile is another option I can look into for you. Let's see how the reseat goes first.

2. Tap **Access Point Names** (APN)
3. Open the menu (three dots, top right) → **Reset to default**
